lesson.applicability: On-demand review of code implementing a declared structured workflow/input boundary.
lesson.cause: Conflating a source-backed review instruction with admission would bypass existing OEEIS activation requirements.
lesson.correction: Bind the existing candidate antibody to a tangible named review prompt and both controls; leave admission and the two-signal gate with their existing owners.
lesson.counterexample: The existing silent-input-coercion spec is explicitly candidate and carries separate harmful and repaired code fixtures.
lesson.evidence_excerpt:
Refuses parsers and workflow runners that silently coerce malformed input types
  (e.g. wrapping a bare scalar into a nullary operation) or silently filter out
  invalid items rather than emitting a typed refusal.
lesson.exceptions: An epitope sighting alone is not a defect or admission. Schema-authorized normalization is benign; no prompt instruction supplies an independent host danger signal.
lesson.failed_claim: An antibody name or a newly generated instruction automatically establishes an admitted executable detector.
